chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qad-dah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and asked: 'O Messenger of God, what is knowledge?' He replied: 'Silence (listening attentively).' The man asked: 'Then what?' He replied: 'Listening to it.' The man asked: 'Then what?' He replied: 'Retaining it (memorizing/remembering).' The man asked: 'Then what?' He replied: 'Acting upon it.' The man asked: 'Then what?' He replied: 'Then spreading it.'
ai.seo_question: What are the five stages of knowledge in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal delineates the epistemological hierarchy of knowledge, moving from passive reception (silence and listening) to active internalization (retention) and externalization (practice and dissemination). In Shia scholarly tradition, this sequence underscores that true 'Ilm is incomplete without 'Amal, reflecting the Imams' emphasis on the unity of knowledge and action as the path to spiritual perfection. The final stage of 'Nashr' (sharing) highlights the communal responsibility of scholars to preserve and transmit the divine message.
